title: Decisive local fuel cut for the layered dividing CIPS condensates: an absorbing fuel moat around one body kills it within 25-50 t on 12 of 12 targets (seeds 0, 1, 9), while every neighbour keeps its size
summary: World unchanged (20261026T1100-c40-cips-layered-divide-claim/world.py). From one t=12000 state per seed I branched a fed twin and one arm per target for the 4 bodies with the farthest nearest neighbours: kF=0 in a disk of radius 0.6x the nearest-neighbour distance (26-27 px) and the fuel set to 0 every step in the annulus 16 px <= r <= that radius (an absorbing moat that stops fuel diffusing in). Every target (196-258 px) is gone (e>0.5 area 0) at t=12025-12050 on seeds 0, 1 and 9; the other three targets in each arm stay within 10% of their fed size, and 14-15 bodies outside the cut survive in every arm. Without the moat (kF=0 disk only, 0.75x nn, seed 9; and c40's 20261026T1238 finding) fuel diffuses into the disk (mean F there only falls 0.82 -> 0.64) and only 1 of 4 targets dies; 3 persist as remnants of 21-29% of fed size for 3000 t. So each body depends on its own fuel supply, and the dependence is produced by the dynamics: the enzyme's only source is a uniform turnover that does not depend on F or on the body; the body is held only by its drift up the product, which needs catalysis on the fuel.

finding.operator: local fuel cut with an absorbing moat (kF=0 in a disk around one body plus F=0 in an annulus 16 px <= r <= 0.6x nearest-neighbour distance) in cooperative CIPS on a consumed, regrowing fuel
finding.control: fed twin and the other targets/bodies in each arm, branched from the same t=12000 state; plain kF=0 disk (no moat) on seed 9 for comparison
finding.result: targets dead (area 0) at t=12025-12050 in 12/12 arms on seeds 0, 1, 9; other targets within 10% of fed size; 14-15 outside bodies kept in every arm. Without the moat: 1/4 dead, 3/4 remnants at 21-29% of fed size for 3000 t

limits: The moat is an imposed fuel sink (it takes fuel from the medium, not only stops regrowth); it is a per-individual supply ablation in the sense of RUBRIC L4c, not a natural starvation. Targets were chosen as the 4 bodies with the farthest nearest neighbours; the moat's outer radius (0.6x nn) leaves 5-10 px of fed medium before each neighbour's edge. One cut time (t=12000), one moat geometry. Body counts here use e>0.5 with periodic merging and min area 10 px, so they differ from labkit's 19 at t=12000.
